notes: All source strings use logical Unicode order.
The isolated original centreline is retained unchanged.
Connected guides are pale font-outline models, not centreline paths.
The single linguistic dot is a separate object, not a tracing-guide dot.
Final connected ـب in عِنَبٌ differs from disconnected final ب after alif in بَابٌ.
No expert handwriting approval or automatic scoring is claimed.

isolated.label: Isolated

strokes.directionHint: down, then left, then gently up
place one dot below the bowl

isolated.methodology: Original HORIZONS educational centreline, unchanged from ba-isolated.json. Original viewBox [0,0,560,400] is cropped to [0,70,560,290]; geometry is unchanged.
isolated.connectionNote: This shape also appears at the end of بَابٌ because alif does not join to the following letter.

initial.label: Initial

strokes.directionHint: Follow the pale model shape; this is not a stroke-order diagram.
Place one dot below the body.

initial.methodology: Correctly shaped Noto Naskh Arabic outlines from logical Unicode, including tatweel as the connecting segment. Body and single dot are separate. Use pale filled shapes, not dotted outlines; no handwriting centreline or stroke-order claim.
initial.connectionNote: Joins the following letter to the left, as in بَيْتٌ.

medial.methodology: Correctly shaped Noto Naskh Arabic outlines from logical Unicode, including tatweel as the connecting segment. Body and single dot are separate. Use pale filled shapes, not dotted outlines; no handwriting centreline or stroke-order claim.
medial.connectionNote: Joins on both sides, as in جَبَلٌ.

final.label: Final, connected

strokes.directionHint: Follow the pale model shape; this is not a stroke-order diagram.

final.methodology: Correctly shaped Noto Naskh Arabic outlines from logical Unicode, including tatweel as the connecting segment. Body and single dot are separate. Use pale filled shapes, not dotted outlines; no handwriting centreline or stroke-order claim.
final.connectionNote: Joins the previous letter on the right, as in عِنَبٌ. In بَابٌ, alif breaks the connection, so the last Baa uses the isolated shape.
